title: Closed as fixed, but QA says it still fails
tests: Status versus evidence. The ticket is Done/Fixed, but a later QA retest shows it still failing with a different error, and nobody reopened it. The model must answer the support question with 'no', and not trust the status field.
request: Support want to know: can we tell the customer this is fixed?

tickets.summary: Password reset email not sent for plus-addressed emails (name+tag@domain)
description: Customers whose email address contains a plus sign (for example alex+bank@example.com) never receive the password reset email. No error is shown to the customer.

comments.author: Priya Nair
body: Root cause: EmailService validated recipient addresses with a regex that rejected '+'. Fixed the validation in PR #201.

comments.author: Priya Nair
body: PR #201 merged, will go out in 3.1.4.

comments.author: Tom Becker
body: Retested on staging with 3.1.4 (build 3.1.4.17): the reset email for test+qa1@example.com still does not arrive.
The SMTP log now shows: "Rejected: 550 5.1.3 Invalid recipient address".
Looks like the email provider is rejecting it now rather than our regex.

comments.author: Marcus Reid
body: The customer asked again today whether this is fixed. Can I tell them yes?

answer_key.expect: No: support should not tell the customer it is fixed.
The ticket is marked Done with resolution Fixed in 3.1.4, but Tom Becker's retest on 2026-09-10 on 3.1.4 staging shows reset emails to plus-addressed recipients still not arriving.
The failure now shows a different error in the SMTP log: '550 5.1.3 Invalid recipient address'.
The remaining failure appears to come from the email provider rejecting the address, a different cause from the regex fixed in PR #201 (Tom says it 'looks like' this; not confirmed).
Nobody reopened the ticket or raised a follow-up after the failed retest, so no one currently owns the remaining problem.
Reopen BANK-377 (or raise a linked new bug), assign an owner to investigate the provider's rejection, and give the customer a holding response rather than confirming a fix.
Says the issue is fixed or that support can confirm the fix to the customer.
answer_key.claim: Yes, the issue is fixed in 3.1.4, so support can tell the customer it is resolved.

answer_key.expect: Claims the ticket has already been reopened or that a follow-up ticket exists.
answer_key.claim: Tom Becker reopened the ticket after the retest.
